sanskrit: yunakta sīrā vi yugā tanota kṛte kṣetre vapateha bījam | virājaḥ śnuṣṭiḥ sabharā asan no nedīya it sṛṇyaḥ pakvam ā yavam ||
english: Yoke the plows, stretch wide the yokes; sow the seed here in the prepared field. May the grace of Virāj be fruitful for us, and may the sickle come ever nearer to the ripened barley.

sanskrit: sīrā yuñjanti kavayo yugā vi tanvate pṛthag dhīrā deveṣu sumnayau | anaḍvāhaḥ puruṣā ye kṛṣanti lāṅgalaṃ phālaṃ sam anajmi sphātyā ||
english: The wise ones yoke the plows, the steadfast ones stretch the yokes apart, seeking the favor of the gods. The bullocks and the men who plow — the plow and the share I anoint with the sphātī-plant for prosperity.

sanskrit: śunaṃ kīnāśo anv etu vāhāñ chunaṃ phālo vinudann etu bhūmim | śunāsīrā haviṣā yo yajātai supippalā oṣadhayaḥ santu tasmai ||
english: May the plowman go behind the draught animals with good fortune; may the share go breaking into the earth with good fortune. Whoever sacrifices to Śunā and Sīra with oblation — may the herbs be well-berried for him.

sanskrit: śunaṃ naro lāṅgalenānaḍudbhir bhagaḥ phālaiḥ kṣetrapatir marudbhiḥ | parjanyo bījam irayedaṃ hinotu śunāsīrā kṛṇutaṃ dhānyeha ||
english: May the men go auspiciously with plow and bullocks; Bhaga with the plowshares, the Lord of the Field with the Maruts. May Parjanya stimulate and impel this seed; O Śunā and Sīra, make the grain plentiful here.

sanskrit: indraḥ sītāṃ ni gṛhṇātu tāṃ pūṣābhi rakṣatu | sā naḥ payasvatī duhām uttarāmuttarāṃ samām ||
english: May Indra take hold of the furrow; may Pūṣan guard her. May she yield milk for us, year after year surpassing the last.

sanskrit: ud asthād rathajid gojid aśvajid dhiraṇyajit sūnṛtayā parīvṛtaḥ | ekacakreṇa savitā rathena- -ūrjo bhāgaiḥ pṛthivīm ety āpṛṇan ||
english: He has arisen — winner of chariots, winner of cattle, winner of horses, winner of gold — encompassed by glad speech. With his single-wheeled chariot, Savitṛ traverses the earth, filling it with portions of vital nourishment.

sanskrit: gavāṃ gṛhāṇāṃ rasam oṣadhīnām anujyeṣṭhaṃ varca āyur vikalpya | sa mā hiṃsīḥ pitarau vardhamāno bhadrāc chreyāṃsam abhi lokam ehi ||
english: Having apportioned in succession the essence of cattle, of houses, of herbs — the luster and the life-span — do not harm my parents as you grow; proceed from the auspicious world toward a yet more excellent one.

sanskrit: yadīdaṃ bhaktaṃ yadi vā vibhaktaṃ kṣetraṃ devānāṃ yadi vā pitṝṇām | yadi sūrya udite yadi vā manuṣyavac chivā no astu pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Whether this field is undivided or divided, whether it belongs to the gods or to the ancestors, whether at sunrise or in human fashion — may the earth be benign to us, and heaven too.

sanskrit: ūrjo vāṃ bhāgo vara ā pṛthivyā devī dvārau brahmaṇā vāṃ dhārayāmi | śivaṃ śagmam avasānaṃ no astu rātaṃ devebhiḥ pitṛbhir manuṣyaiḥ ||
english: Your share is nourishment, O divine pair of doors, the choicest part of the earth; I uphold you both with the sacred word. May our resting-place be auspicious and propitious, the gift granted by the gods, the fathers, and human beings.

sanskrit: viśvāvasos tvā sadanaṃ kulāyaṃ gandharvāso vedhaso mahyam ūcuḥ | sa mā hiṃsīḥ śevadhiṃ yaṃ ta etaṃ śataṃ himāḥ pari dadmo manuṣyam ||
english: The Gandharvas, the wise ones, told me of this abode of Viśvāvasu, this nest. Do not harm this treasure which we hereby entrust to you — a human being — for a hundred winters.

sanskrit: rudrā utse sadam akṣīyamāṇe devā madanti pitaro manuṣyāḥ | ayaṃ bhāgo bhāgapatiś ca devā urvīr astaryāḥ śaradas tarema ||
english: At the ever-inexhaustible spring, the Rudras rejoice, gods and fathers and human beings. This is the share, and the Lord of Shares is present; O gods, may we cross over the wide, unending autumns.

sanskrit: yo asmin yakṣmaḥ puruṣe praviṣṭa iṣitaṃ daivyaṃ sahaḥ | agniṣ ṭaṃ ghṛtabodhano apa skandayatv adhi dūram asmat so anyena sam ṛcchatāṃ tam asmai pra suvāmasi ||
english: Whatever consumption-disease has entered into this man — a power sent forth by the divine — may Agni, awakened by ghee, drive it far away from us. May it unite with another; we dispatch it to that one.

sanskrit: yas tvā yakṣmo deveṣita iṣitaḥ pitṛbhiś ca yaḥ | tasmāt tvā viśve devā muñcantu pary aṃhasaḥ | te te yakṣmam apa skandayantv adhi (…) | (…) ||
english: Whatever consumption-disease was sent by the gods, and whatever was sent by the fathers — from that may all the gods release you from affliction. May they drive your disease away…

sanskrit: yat tvam eno anyakṛtaṃ yad ātmakṛtam āritha | tasmāt tvā viśvā bhūtāni muñcantu pary aṃhasaḥ | tāni te yakṣmam apa skandayantv adhi (…) (…) ||
english: Whatever guilt made by another or made by yourself you have incurred — from that may all beings release you from affliction. May they drive your disease away…

sanskrit: yat tvā sva ādṛśā yad vā cakāra niṣṭyaḥ | tasmāt tvā pṛthivī mātā muñcatu pary aṃhasaḥ | sā te yakṣmam apa skandayatv adhi (…) (…) ||
english: Whatever one of your own kindred has done to you, or whatever an outsider has done — from that may Mother Earth release you from affliction. May she drive your disease away…

sanskrit: apaskandena haviṣā yakṣmaṃ te nāśayāmasi | tad agnir āha tad u soma āha bṛhaspatiḥ savitā tad indraḥ | te te yakṣmam apa skandayantv adhi dūram asmat so anyena sam ṛcchatāṃ tam asmai pra suvāmasi ||
english: With the apaskanda-oblation we destroy your disease. So spoke Agni, so spoke Soma, so Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, and Indra. May they drive your disease far away from us. May it unite with another; we dispatch it to that one.
